title: Phase-bound workers with durable repository ownership
outcomes: Choose a supported worker topology with separate protocol, fixture and live proof levels.

in: Compare fresh workers, persistent turn overrides and subagents using versioned local protocol and actual existing workspace/context/process guards
out: New user-facing Codex task per phase
boundaries: One canonical repository controller, one task workspace, frozen phase profiles and exclusive writer; reviewer read-only

decision_rights: Authorize execution and choose model; GO on 2026-09-13
Implement bounded contract choices and document compatibility behavior

constraints: Retain fresh ephemeral CLI workers per phase as the supported baseline. Each phase reconstructs context from canonical .go and verifies ownership before payload.
Protocol capability alone is not an implemented or live-confirmed Go adapter. Record exact local binary version and source schema digests.

Persistent turn overrides persist to later turns in the inspected protocol; any future adapter must explicitly select each phase and retain exact thread identity. Ephemeral sessions cannot be assumed to survive process loss.
Subagents require their own verified profile, process ownership, scope, context and recovery adapter; defer without making this a baseline dependency.
No mid-turn switching or active frozen-profile edits. The same task worktree survives safe phase transitions. Only canonical controller publishes; critic is read-only.

quality_attributes.scenario: Switch build critic repair with different profiles
quality_attributes.measure: New task worktrees or concurrent writers
Missing canonical context or lost feedback
Protocol or fixture proof mislabeled as live runtime confirmation

risks: Versioned app-server protocol is evidence for this inspected binary, not a promise across all installations.
Fixture workers validate control boundaries but do not attest provider execution identity.
